one_month_reasoning: No Jabil-specific scheduled event falls in the window to 2026-11-01: Q4 FY26 results and the FY27 guide were released 2026-09-30 (stock fell ~4% despite a beat and above-consensus guide), and Q1 FY27 results are due around mid-December. The main event in the window is the late-October hyperscaler earnings round (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon), whose capex commentary moves AI hardware names like JBL in both directions; I have no edge on its sign. Post-earnings drift after a beat is mildly positive, but it is offset by the negative reaction on the day and the sector de-risking seen since June. I therefore center the distribution on today's $304.41 with a symmetric lognormal at sigma ~13.5% (47% annual vol / 3.5), with slightly fatter tails for the hyperscaler capex prints.

fair_value.method: Blend of 15.5x FY28 core EPS of ~$19.50 (~$302, 60%) and a 5.5% FCF yield on FY28 adjusted FCF of ~$1.7B over ~102M shares (~$303, 40%). Both haircut the AI-driven growth and the multiple versus bullish consensus targets (~$441-454), because core EPS leaves out stock comp/amortization and the 2027 numbers sit on hyperscaler capex.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Aug-2028) core EPS ~$19.50 x 15.5x forward multiple at Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide $17.55 grown ~11%, about half of FY27's 34% guided growth. Growth slows as the AI ramp laps (FY27 AI revenue guided +54% to $22.1B), ramp costs are back-end loaded, and peers point to choppy hyperscaler order flow; buybacks add ~3%.

Stock re-rated to ~23x NTM (near a 10-year high) in mid-2026 and has since de-rated to ~17x the FY27 guide after the Goldman PT cut and Zacks downgrade. Pre-AI history was low-teens for EMS. 15.5x assumes a further partial de-rating as the AI growth rate peaks, which is a skeptic's discount to today's ~17x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 adjusted FCF ~$1.7B / ~102M diluted shares = ~$16.7/share, capitalized at a 5.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: ~6% above the FY27 guide. Kept modest because inventory days (64 net, ~82 gross) are above the 55-60 target, receivable sales and securitization (~$720M outstanding) flatter operating cash flow, and capex runs at 1.5-2% of revenue for 4M sq ft of new capacity.
106.0M at Aug-2026 less ~4% from continued buybacks (FY26 buyback was $1.06B).
The stock's FY27 adj FCF yield today is ~5.0% ($1.6B / ~$32B market cap). Investment-grade debt at ~4.2-4.75% coupons means the equity yield needs a cyclical/concentration premium, so I require 5.5%.

bear.story: Hyperscaler capex digestion in 2027 (or one of the 3 hyperscaler customers, the second expected to exceed 10% of revenue, insources or shifts share). The FY27 guide is cut, FY28 EPS goes flat at ~$16, inventory (already 64 days) has to be worked down, FCF disappoints, and the multiple compresses to ~12x as in past EMS down-cycles. Roughly a retest of the $189.60 52-week low.

base.story: Jabil roughly delivers the $17.55 FY27 guide (it has a record of beating its guides) and the FY28 outlook implies ~10-12% growth. AI growth decelerates from +54%, the multiple drifts from ~17x to ~15.5-16x forward, and EPS growth roughly offsets the de-rating. The stock is about flat.

bull.story: AI capex stays above $1.2T, 6%+ margins prove durable, the FY28 guide is ~$21-22 and the market pays ~20x as in mid-2026. That reaches about the June 2026 high and the ~$441-454 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$205 the stock would trade at under 12x the $17.55 FY27 guide, i.e. a pre-AI EMS multiple. That level is most consistent with the market pricing a guidance cut from hyperscaler capex digestion or a lost large AI program, not ordinary 47%-vol noise. It also sits just above the $189.60 52-week low; a break there would confirm the AI earnings step-up is being unwound.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler AI capex through 2027-2028; JBL's FY27 AI revenue guide is $22.1B (+54%), about half of revenue
Customer concentration: top 5 customers are ~36% of revenue; a second hyperscaler will exceed 10% in FY27, and Apple remains large
Working-capital quality: inventory above target (64 net days), receivable sales and securitization (~$720M outstanding), contract assets up ~39% YTD

Execution on 4M sq ft of new capacity with back-end-loaded margins
reasoning: Basic facts: FY26 core EPS was $13.09 and revenue $36.0B (+21%). The FY27 guide of $17.55 core EPS on $44.5B revenue, $1.6B adj FCF and a 6.1% core margin was above consensus ($16.92 / $42.93B), yet the stock fell ~4% on 2026-09-30. It sits ~29% below the June high at ~17x the FY27 guide. As the skeptic I looked for what makes the consensus (~$441-454 targets) wrong. I found no short-seller report, litigation or accounting allegation of substance. Credit is investment-grade: the Jan-2026 notes priced at 4.2%/4.75%, net debt is ~$1.64B and there are no covenant concerns. Real bear points: (1) the earnings step-up is concentrated in AI/cloud for a few hyperscalers, and peers (Celestica: 3 customers >63% of sales, stock down 33% from highs) show how violently this group de-rates on capex fears; (2) working-capital quality: inventory above target, receivables sold and securitized, contract assets rising, buybacks partly debt-funded; (3) steady insider selling by the CEO (~$2.7M at ~$287) and the chairman, routine but not supportive; (4) the market already doesn't believe the guide: a beat-and-raise sold off, Goldman cut its PT to $375 and Zacks downgraded, which shows a multiple compressing as growth peaks. Weighed honestly, Jabil has a record of beating guidance and the stock already prices some skepticism (17x vs ~23x peak), so I do not forecast a collapse. Fair value ~$302 (P/E and FCF-yield methods agree), about flat to spot. Scenarios: bear $195 (25%), base $310 (50%), bull $440 (25%), modeled as a lognormal mixture. The result has a median of ~$305 and wide tails consistent with 47% realized vol (fatter left tail than a typical large-cap because of AI-cycle and concentration risk). P(>= spot) is ~0.52.
